sentences.text: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has become a key figure in the current AI era.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: Artificial intelligence (AI) firm Anthropic just released the required paperwork ahead of its long-anticipated debut on the US stock market.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: The 335-page document included fresh details of how the Claude chatbot owner makes money, what it spends that money on and who it is controlled by.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: Anthropic also detailed some of the risks it claimed AI technology poses, including how it could take human lives.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: That information sat alongside the many purported benefits of the technology.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: Here are five key points worth highlighting from the filing.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: Every public company has to tell potential investors how things could go wrong.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: Anthropic's "risk factors" were unique, also disclosing how the AI technology it is developing could doom humanity as a whole.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: "Sufficiently advanced AI systems could, if not developed, deployed, and operated with appropriate safeguards, oversight, and security measures, pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity," Anthropic said.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: It noted that less than a year ago, a hacking group Anthropic believed to be sponsored by China "manipulated" Claude to successfully intrude on a number of institutions, including large technology companies, financial institutions, chemical manufacturing companies and government agencies.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: But Anthropic said its success is dependent on its ability to constantly "develop, improve, and deploy the most advanced, capable, and useful AI models".
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: One of the most significant risks to that ability is Anthropic's access to infrastructure it needs, including computer chips and data centres, to build, train and operate the models that underpin its technology.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: Anthropic has yet to disclose a target share price for its stock listing.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: The company is widely expected to debut with a market valuation of $2 trillion or more, making it the largest stock listing in history.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: But the figure will be heavily influenced by its financial performance.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: Anthropic lost $80.7bn (£60bn) in the first half of this year, double what it lost across 2025 altogether.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: The company's overall revenue was $16.2bn for the six-month period.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: Revenues are rising rapidly, but the firm has a long way to go before it breaks even.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: Troy Hooper, co-head of equity capital markets at Mergermarket, said Anthropic's revenue growth is "exceptional".
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: But investors are "less forgiving" of tech companies promising huge future returns than they were even months ago, he added.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: Anthropic's debt picture is also unclear given it has a huge amount of accounting charges related to certain forms of investment.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: "As a result, investors do not yet have a clear view of Anthropic's underlying profitability or whether its rate of cash generation is sufficient to support the business as it scales," Hooper added.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: Despite losing money, Anthropic has heaps of cash lying about.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: At $131.6bn, almost all of its cash in hand is defined as "working capital", meaning it can use the money to fund its operations day-to-day.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: Currently, Anthropic has more cash on hand than Meta and Google combined.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: Anthropic's costs could rise as it faces fierce competition for top staff and computing power from other AI giants.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: The leasing of data centres alone is set to cost the company $321.4bn through agreements struck so far this year.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: Hooper said such large costs are expected to grow.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: Even with this kind of cash, it won't be enough to maintain its business growth.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: Any investors in Anthropic "will be paying for future dominance, not present-day economics", he said.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: Anthropic sees boundless ways it can sell its technology to customers.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: A large portion of its current business comes from just 250 major enterprise customers, which it says have paid it at least $10m in the past year.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: An even smaller number, just five enterprise customers, make up a quarter of its current business.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: Michael Monaghan, portfolio manager of Founder ETF, pointed out that "many top Anthropic customers have no long-term contract".
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: The company's level of business concentration leaves Anthropic dependent on a small fraction of its paying customers to support its growth, with no guarantee it will continue.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: Anthropic also has enterprise relationships with the likes of Google and Amazon, both of which are also investors in the company "and competitors", creating potential business conflicts in the future, Monaghan noted.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: Anthropic said its overall enterprise customer base has grown rapidly, going from roughly 1,500 customers last year to almost 12,000 this year.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: Part of its growth strategy is offering Claude tools for free before working to "convert these users into paying customers over time".
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: The strategy has led to Claude seeing "the fastest enterprise adoption of any technology in history", the company claimed.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: For all of the risks Anthropic has said AI poses, it also reiterated its claim AI will produce an "extraordinary" amount of good.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: "Achieving our mission means the world gains the enormous benefits of frontier AI while mitigating the most significant risks," the company said.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: Decades of scientific progress could be condensed into years, accelerating drug discovery, disease detection, and the delivery of personalised therapy.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: Anthropic said AI could provide individually tailored education and expert financial and legal advice, advance power grids and battery design for greater efficiency and reliability and help the "developing world" build more technological capabilities.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: "Ultimately, we believe frontier AI will help drive global economic growth," the company said.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: Amazon Prime Air is expanding to 500 US towns and cities Nature lover Ashley Schmidt no longer spends much time in her garden, in the Dallas suburb of North Garland.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: She's also given up on cycling to the local parks where she previously enjoyed taking close-up photos of the bugs, lizards and toads.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: It's all because she can't stand the sound of the delivery drones that fly overhead, depositing her neighbours' online orders.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: "They emit this very annoying buzz.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: It triggers my fight or flight response," says the 44-year-old administrative assistant.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: "You can hear the drones on approach and you can hear them inside your home when they pass directly overhead and then you hear them as they leave," she says.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Amazon says it is working to reduce the noise of its drone fleet Schmidt is one of a growing number of people living with the noise of drones dispatched by companies including Amazon and Walmart as they seek to speed up home deliveries.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Delivery drone services, not long ago a novelty, are becoming part of everyday life for many people in the US.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Among them, Amazon Prime Air is in the process of expanding deliveries to nearly 500 cities and towns, delivering items that fit into a space the size of a shoe box.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: It has also launched to customers in and around Darlington in the north of England.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Smaller drone delivery services are popping up too: in some US cities, customers can order flying treats from their local pizza joint or ice cream parlour.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Even in cities where noise is already a steady part of life, the sound of drones seems to irk in a particular way.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: While the steady passing of traffic might blend into the background, the sudden whine of a drone's rotors can pierce the everyday hum.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: The sound tends to be "particularly noticeable, even when overall sound levels are relatively low," says Antonio Torija Martinez, professor in acoustic engineering and psychoacoustics at the University of Salford.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Unlike planes, drones operate at low altitudes and may fly directly over residential areas.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: "They can expose communities that have not previously experienced significant aircraft noise, and who may therefore be more sensitive to changes in their local soundscape," says Torija Martinez.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: He points to research showing that people respond strongly to a noise when they consider the source to be "novel, intrusive or frequent".
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: People who benefit from a drone delivery service, for example, may be less bothered by the noise.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: The FAA says operators and local community leaders have primary responsibility for addressing any community concerns.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Greenjets encloses some of the blades on its drone inside a pod Might better technology muffle the irritating buzz?
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: One startup, Greenjets, set out to tackle both "noise level and the frequency of that noise," as Darren James, future technologies lead at the company, puts it.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: The London-based business has designed a propulsion system it claims can reduce drone noise by at least two thirds.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: While standard drones use spinning propellers that slice through open air, creating that high-pitched buzz, Greenjets encloses spinning blades inside a pod, to muffle the sound and direct the noise away from the ground.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Its system also quietens things down through slower rotor speed and by using materials that reduce vibration noise.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Making quieter drones isn't just about keeping the noise down for neighbours who are already sick of airborne deliveries.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Greenjets' low-noise tech has been used by police and harbour security teams in Germany.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: It has also helped conservationists in Africa, who are seeking to track poachers from above without being detected.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Battlefield drone operators also have good reason to keep the noise down, to avoid alerting the enemy of the approach of their unmanned vehicles.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: "There are some efforts to reduce the sound of drones.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: The US Special Forces are interested, at an experimental stage," says Robert Tollast, a research fellow at Whitehall think tank The Royal United Services Institute (RUSI).
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: But he stresses that drone speed, rather than stealthiness, tends to come first for larger drones used in the war between Russia and Ukraine.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: "Make it faster, not less quiet, seems to be the approach," says Tollast.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Sharrow Engineering developed twisted propellers that reduce noise For Detroit-based entrepreneur, Greg Sharrow, it was the challenge of broadcasting a classical music performance back in 2012 that set him on the path to quieter drone design.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: He needed to film a violinist from a tricky angle and a drone seemed the only solution – expect that it would be far too noisy.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: As a starting point, "I knew that most of the noise from the drone was coming from the propeller, not the motor," he says.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Specifically, it was the tips of the blades that he realised were creating the noise as they swiped through the air.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: "I asked myself a very simple question, what would a tipless propeller look like and how would it function?" The result was to create a propeller with twisted loop-shaped blades with no points.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: It turned out it was easier to test his propeller in water than it was to repeatedly fly a drone, which led Sharrow to initially develop a less noisy boat propeller.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Now, however, his company, Sharrow Engineering, is focusing on developing "ultra-quiet" drone rotors.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: "We have validated that the technology works in drone applications and that it is dramatically quieter," says Sharrow.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Companies at the forefront of drone deliveries say they are also working to reduce the noise of their fleets.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: A spokesperson for Amazon says it has made "measurable sound improvements" to its drones and its latest designs use custom-designed propellers "that produce almost half the perceived sound of the prior generation, with a milder tone".
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Drone maker Wing, which provides its vehicles for Walmart deliveries, says its propellers are designed to minimise noise.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: It also varies its flight paths to prevent repeated overflights over any single home or neighbourhood.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: For Schmidt, fed up with the noise of drones, the only truly satisfactory solution would be to halt drone deliveries in her area.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: "I would like them to completely stop until they figure out how their services stop being a nuisance," she says.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing Until a few years ago many of us may have been blissfully unaware of what a data centre was.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: These giant, warehouse-like buildings power virtually all our internet activity, from our web searches and emails to movie downloads and online banking.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: They are at the heart of the AI boom, housing the advanced computer chips and servers needed to run services like ChatGPT and Claude.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: But the speed at which they're growing, the enormous amount of electricity they consume and concerns about their environmental impact are fuelling a public backlash around the world.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: In the US, they've become a huge issue ahead of the midterm elections on 3 November, with both Republicans and opposition Democrats coming out against their development.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: It's putting opponents of data centre expansion on a collision course with US President Donald Trump, who has dismissed the pushback as a "sick conspiracy", even as public anger grows.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: Here's what you need to know about the data centre boom, and why opposition is growing.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: There are about 12,250 data centres around the world, according to Data Center Map , external , a company that tracks both operational and pre-operational sites.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: That's up sharply from 2021, when there were around 8,000 , external operational sites.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: As the chart below shows, data centres are most densely clustered in the US which has 4,767 sites.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: It is followed by Europe, where the UK and Germany lead.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: Data centres have typically been located near to cities where it's easier to access high voltage power lines or water resources for cooling.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: But as they get bigger, more are being built in rural areas.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: But when it comes to actual capacity, the US is ahead by a much larger margin, with China in second place and Europe lagging far behind.

sentences.text: Marcus Perkins said rising costs were making it harder for salons to employ staff and train apprentices After 22 years running a salon, Marcus Perkins says he is increasingly worried about the future of the hair and beauty industry.

sentences.text: Rising costs are making it harder for businesses to employ staff and invest in apprenticeships, he says, while more salons are turning to self-employed models to survive.
sentences.article_title: Salon owners urge Budget VAT cut as staffing pressures grow

sentences.text: "Seeing salons close on the high street is very scary," he said.
sentences.article_title: Salon owners urge Budget VAT cut as staffing pressures grow

sentences.text: Luckily it hasn't happened yet but who knows what the future holds?" Perkins is among more than 2,000 salon owners who have signed an open letter calling on the Chancellor John Healey to cut VAT on hair and beauty services from 20% to 10% in this week's Budget.
sentences.article_title: Salon owners urge Budget VAT cut as staffing pressures grow

sentences.text: The letter is backed by the British Hair Consortium (BHC), which argues rising business costs are placing increasing pressure on traditional salon employers.
sentences.article_title: Salon owners urge Budget VAT cut as staffing pressures grow

sentences.text: However, the industry has also seen growing numbers of stylists move into self-employed arrangements, with hairdressers often renting a chair within a salon rather than being directly employed.

sentences.text: With salon ownership perceived to be out of reach for many, self-employment offered independence, flexibility and higher earnings, industry research suggested , external .
sentences.article_title: Salon owners urge Budget VAT cut as staffing pressures grow

sentences.text: A Treasury spokesperson said hair and beauty businesses played an important role in supporting jobs, apprenticeships and thriving high streets.

sentences.text: Rosey Greenwood was asked to pay £1,906 because she took more than five minutes to pay for parking "I was completely on edge, every single day," said Rosey Greenwood.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: "I had letters coming through - I had debt collectors after me." Two years ago, Rosey was being told to pay £1,906 because she had taken too long to pay for parking.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: Rosey had paid every single time she parked at the Copeland Street car park in Derby, and had bank records to prove it.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: But Rosey had unknowingly broken the car park's terms and conditions, which stipulated that drivers must pay within five minutes of entering.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: Rosey could not afford to pay £1,906 - she was due to get married and also saving up to buy her first home.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: As she prepared to fight the case in court, her fiance emailed the BBC and asked us to "shed some light" on what was happening .
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: The case was then raised in Parliament , external by Derby North MP Catherine Atkinson, who described the charges - which had caught out countless other motorists - as a "five-minute rip-off charge".
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: The parking sector subsequently banned the five-minute payment rule by updating its code of practice , external , but the government is going further by bringing in a statutory Private Parking Code of Practice.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: "These charges leave people feeling ripped off and out of pocket, so I'm putting a stop to them," Prime Minister Andy Burnham said , external on Monday.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: But will the new code actually put the brakes on "rip-off" parking charges?
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: Prime Minister Andy Burnham said parking charges left people "feeling ripped off" The government's new Private Parking Code of Practice was laid out in Parliament on Tuesday.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: It sets out standards that parking operators must follow.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: Housing and communities minister Florence Eshalomi said , external the new code "will give drivers a range of rights and protections to make these unfair practices a thing of the past".
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: The code is now subject to a 40-day period of parliamentary scrutiny, during which MPs and peers can object before it is formally issued.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: The code will then come into force 21 calendar days from the point of issue.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: The five-minute payment rule - as stipulated on this sign - had already been banned by the parking sector itself In places, the code appears to be very similar to the private parking sector's existing code of practice , external .
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: For example, Eshalomi said drivers would "now have a guaranteed minimum five minutes to decide whether to park", known as the consideration period.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: However, the sector's code already gives drivers a minimum consideration period of five minutes, so this does not appear to be new.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: The government's code also gives drivers a 10-minute grace period , external in which to leave a car park following the end of their permitted stay.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: However, the sector's code already gives drivers a 10-minute grace period, so this does not appear to be new either.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: The government's code sets the maximum parking charge at £100, or £60 if paid within a fortnight.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: This is also the same as in the sector's code.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: The government's code states charges should be reduced to £20 on appeal , external under four circumstances: not displaying a parking permit despite having a valid one, entering the wrong vehicle registration into a parking machine, not entering a registration at all, and not displaying a Blue Badge despite having one.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: The sector's code already said charges should be reduced to £20 under those circumstances.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: Parking operators will also still be allowed to add a £70 debt recovery fee , external to each parking charge if drivers do not pay, as well as court fees and legal costs.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: In contrast, the sector's code said these charges should be reduced to £20.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: The government's code says parking operators who do not comply will lose access to DVLA vehicle keeper data, meaning they will no longer be able to issue parking charges.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: This is meant to happen already, because parking operators need to be members of one of two trade associations in order to access DVLA data, and they can theoretically lose their membership if they break the rules.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: Campaigners claim this has not happened in practice, but the government insists it will happen in future.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: There will also be what the government describes as a "fully independent Scrutiny and Oversight Board".
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: Jack Cousens, head of roads policy at the AA, said the benefit of the new code was that it was backed by the government, rather than the parking sector itself.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: "That means, if there are any changes to be made, it will come via the government and indeed via the independent scrutiny panel," he added.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: "Up until now, the private industry have held the pen on changing the code of practice.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: Now the pen is firmly in the hand of the government." Lynda Eagan does not believe the new code will lead to fewer parking charge notices being issued Both the AA and RAC have welcomed the statutory code of practice - which they campaigned for - but believe it does not go far enough.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: For example, the AA believes there needs to be a single and independent appeals process.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: "Drivers need to have confidence that when they are making their representations, it's being heard by an independent body, as opposed to the private parking operators and their trade bodies marking their own homework," Cousens said.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: The AA also believes the government needs to find an alternative to debt recovery fees and charges, which often "spiral" into the threat of court action and County Court Judgments.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: This was how Rosey was asked to pay a total of £1,906 for 10 parking charges, and also how Hannah Robinson was asked to pay £11,390 .
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: The RAC shares the same concerns.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: "We've long called for the banning of debt recovery fees being added on top of parking charge notices, and a single independent appeals body to replace the two industry-run ones, but neither have been included [in the code] which is disappointing," head of policy Simon Williams said.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: The government said it was "consulting as soon as possible next year on private parking debt recovery fees, including on whether to cut an existing £70 cap or scrap the fees altogether".
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: Parking campaigner Lynda Eagan, who helped Rosey, is sceptical about how much has changed.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: "I've been screaming at the TV every time I see someone saying 'we've got these new things'," she said.

sentences.text: Mohammed Ashim is paid to film his hands at work Mohammed Ashim has been cutting hair and trimming beards for four years in Bengaluru.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: But recently the 22-year old has been strapping a camera to his head to record his work.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: The camera only records his hands and fingers - his client's faces are blurred out.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "The routine is simple, but you have to be disciplined about how you move.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: The operations team taught me that my hands always have to stay cleanly inside the frame, the lighting has to be sharp, and I can't tilt my head too abruptly while working." He wears the camera for five or six hours a day.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "It's good money, but honestly, the feeling of doing something this futuristic is what keeps me excited.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: I never imagined my razor techniques would be useful to a global tech company," says Ashim.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: He is one of hundreds of thousands of workers across the world paid to record their activities.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Ashim's footage is collected by a local company, which might have hundreds of people filming their work.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: That video is then sold on to technology companies and research organisations who use it to train artificial intelligence - in particular so-called physical AI, a type of artificial intelligence that can control robots in the real world.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Rashdan Technologies collects and processes such human generated data.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "Every robotics company, every frontier AI lab, has a specific kind of data they want: industrial tasks, agriculture, household chores, small business work like pottery, garment-making, embroidery, candle-making.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: We go wherever the task is," says co-founder and CEO Shahil Baig.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: His company pays $5 to $10 (£3.74; £7.47) for eight to 10 hours of recorded work.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "For a lot of these people, that's meaningful," Baig says.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Making sure workers give their consent and are comfortable with the process is important, he says.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "We record hands, not faces, and where multi-camera rigs do capture more of the body or environment, we blur faces out.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: No names, no contact details, nothing that identifies them personally goes into what we hand off." But his customers are getting more demanding.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "Now clients are asking for four to six cameras rigged around a person's head to cover the entire scene, not just the hands.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "Getting someone to agree to one small camera is one conversation.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Getting them to agree to wearing what's effectively a five-camera headset is a completely different, and harder, one.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: We pay more for that tier of data collection because of what we're asking of people." And the industry is becoming more crowded, Agarwal expects dozens more competitors to emerge in India this year.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Shahil Baig expects dozens more firms to start collecting video of workers Why is such data so important?
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: If you want robots to navigate the real world, they can't just be trained inside computer simulations, argues Manish Agarwal, the founder of Humyn Labs, which collects and processes human-generated data.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Most of that data comes from video, but sometimes collectors wear hardware on their hands and fingers to capture physical contact.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "Physical tasks require high-quality signals involving limb movements, fingers, wrists, elbows, shoulders and dynamic force application.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: For example: applying the correct grip force so a plastic bottle doesn't crumble versus a steel glass," he says.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: And until recently, that data was not available.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "There is no existing internet archive of embodied human activity - no dataset of a kitchen being cleaned, or a car being assembled by hands that know exactly how much force to apply.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: That data has to be captured from scratch, in the real world, across diverse environments," says Agarwal, whose company has bases in Bangalore and San Francisco.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: At the moment his firm has 96,000 data collectors across countries in Latin America and Southeast Asia.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Humyn Labs filters the thousands of hours of video supplied by those collectors, selecting the most useful content.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: The operators of Newby Island landfill have been ordered to take action over odours Milpitas, an affluent city in California's Silicon Valley tech hub, has an odour problem.

sentences.text: For decades, residents have had to endure rank smells wafting from industrial sites, among them a 342-acre landfill.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "When I first moved here, I could not open my window for over 10 years," says Chia-Ling Kong, an engineer for a tech firm who lives around half a mile from the dump.

sentences.text: While things have got better in recent years, Kong says she and her neighbours must still contend with around "two or three hours of bad smells a day".

sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Kong is optimistic a data-driven approach will make a difference.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "Hopefully with this continuous monitoring, it makes it easier to pinpoint problems at the moment it starts." The operators of the landfill say they are committed to operating it safely and protecting air quality.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Just like in Milpitas, where Kong is part of a citizen's campaign against the odours, communities around the world are raising a stink about bad smells making day-to-day life miserable.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Sometimes a rubbish dump is to blame, or it might be a sewage treatment works, or a reeking factory.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Many countries have no regulations in place dictating how to manage smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: In the US, for example, the Environmental Protection Agency does not regulate environmental odours as a pollutant.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: This leaves states and local governments to take charge of the issue.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: But this can be expensive and some operators opt for simpler and cheaper solutions.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Residents in Des Moines, Iowa, have long complained of the so-called Eastside Funk, a putrid scent that residents report drifts over parts of the city.

sentences.text: But that's not that realistic." The Spanish company's monitors are an example of so-called electronic noses that make it easier to detect smells.

sentences.text: Eddie Lever was able to leave his tenancy more easily because of the Renters' Rights Act When the Renters' Rights Act came into force in May it was described as the biggest change for tenants in England in a generation, giving more stability and security to the millions of people who rent from private landlords.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: The legislation has also prompted a shake-up of the student rental market, which has posed challenges for landlords as it allows people to leave a tenancy rather than being tied in for the full academic year.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Eddie Lever had finished his first year at the University of Exeter when he decided the course wasn't for him.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: The 20-year-old wanted to switch to studying international relations at the University of York but had already organised his house for the upcoming year.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: The tenancy was signed and had started.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: But because of changes in the Renters' Rights Act, Eddie only had to give two months' notice before he could leave and stop paying rent.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: The legislation ended fixed-term tenancies - where renters are tied in to contracts for a specific number of months.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: For students, previously contracts were generally for the full academic year.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Instead, properties are now rented on a rolling basis, which means tenants pay rent weekly or monthly with no fixed end date.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: University-owned halls of residence and Purpose-Built Student Accommodation are exempt , external and can still offer fixed-term contracts so this change primarily affects students renting from a private landlord.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: "If the Renters' Rights Act wasn't a thing, I don't think I would have been able to move universities because I would have been locked into the full [year] contract," Eddie explains.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Fortunately, Eddie had a friend who was looking for a room who was able to take his place so his housemates could sign a new tenancy.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: He acknowledges the situation would have been more difficult for his housemates if there wasn't someone who could take his room.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: However, Eddie thinks the benefits for students are worth this risk.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: "If you were to fall out with your flatmates or if you decide that university is not for you, being locked into a full-term contract can be really prohibitive financially," he says.

sentences.text: "So without that flexibility, people can really be locked into situations that they don't necessarily want to be in." Lewis Wilson, vice president for higher education at the National Union of Students, says this flexibility means students can also save money on rent by moving home for the summer.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: While previously, many student rental contracts ran into the summer after courses had finished, students can now choose to move out earlier if they want.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Wilson says students also benefit from wider changes in the act, which bans landlords in England from evicting tenants without a reason.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.article_title: Chancellor says he will cut 'pointless paperwork' to save businesses up to £800m

sentences.text: Households will need to earn less than £110,000 to qualify for the government's new loan scheme for first-time buyers, or £140,000 for homes bought in London.
sentences.article_title: Earnings limit of up to £140K for first-time buyers loan scheme

sentences.text: As first reported by The Times , external , the earnings limits are expected to be confirmed at the Budget next week.
sentences.article_title: Earnings limit of up to £140K for first-time buyers loan scheme

sentences.text: The Your First Home scheme will offer government-backed equity loans worth 20% of new-build properties in England bought from participating developers.
sentences.article_title: Earnings limit of up to £140K for first-time buyers loan scheme

sentences.text: The loans, which will also be subject to an initial interest-free period, are designed to help people buy a home with deposits as low as 2.5%.
sentences.article_title: Earnings limit of up to £140K for first-time buyers loan scheme

sentences.text: Previous schemes to help first-time buyers did not restrict eligibility by income but faced criticism for stoking house prices by allowing relatively wealthy households to borrow more.
sentences.article_title: Earnings limit of up to £140K for first-time buyers loan scheme

sentences.text: Unveiling the Your First Home Scheme at last month's Labour conference, Prime Minister Andy Burnham said it would focus on those who "really need support".
sentences.article_title: Earnings limit of up to £140K for first-time buyers loan scheme

sentences.text: The Times reported that ministers had initially decided to set the earnings limits at £90,000 for homes outside outside London and £110,000 in the capital, before concluding this would deny access to too many middle-earning couples, such as teachers and nurses.
sentences.article_title: Earnings limit of up to £140K for first-time buyers loan scheme

sentences.text: The government has also argued that the scheme will help to boost housebuilding, after ministers conceded they are set to miss a target to build 1.5 million homes in England by the next election.
sentences.article_title: Earnings limit of up to £140K for first-time buyers loan scheme

sentences.text: Labour has said the scheme will be funded by within existing government budgets, but is yet to provide details of which other areas will see their spending cut.
sentences.article_title: Earnings limit of up to £140K for first-time buyers loan scheme

sentences.text: Developers taking part in the scheme will also be asked to contribute towards running costs.
sentences.article_title: Earnings limit of up to £140K for first-time buyers loan scheme

sentences.text: The Home Builders Federation, which represents developers, has welcomed  the plans and urged the government to move quickly to set up the scheme.
sentences.article_title: Earnings limit of up to £140K for first-time buyers loan scheme

sentences.text: The Conservatives have however branded the proposals a "colossal admission of failure" of Labour's housebuilding record, and expressed concerns that the new developer levy could push up the price of new homes.
sentences.article_title: Earnings limit of up to £140K for first-time buyers loan scheme

sentences.text: Like the Help to Buy scheme launched under the Conservative-Liberal Democrat coalition government, the scheme will use equity loans, which are linked to changes in the value of properties they are used to purchase.
sentences.article_title: Earnings limit of up to £140K for first-time buyers loan scheme

sentences.text: That scheme, which initially ran between 2013 and 2021, enabled all home purchasers to put down a 5% deposit on a newly built home worth up to £600,000.

sentences.text: Green leader Zack Polanski has faced criticism over his response to the Zionism motion Labour is set to decide whether to end power-sharing with Green councillors after demanding they disown their party's policy that Zionism is a form of racism.

sentences.article_title: Green councillors face Labour deadline to disown Zionism policy

sentences.text: Anthony Lee and his wife Laura pleaded guilty at Southwark Crown Court on Thursday The Conservatives' former director of campaigning and his wife have received suspended prison sentences after they admitted to cheating at gambling by placing bets on the date of the 2024 general election.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: Anthony Lee used "inside information" emerging from a private meeting called by then-Prime Minister Rishi Sunak to bet on the general election date months before it took place, Southwark Crown Court heard.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: Lee and his wife Laura stood to win more than £23,000 had their cheating not been uncovered, the court heard.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: Lee was sentenced to 10 months and two weeks' imprisonment, suspended for 12 months, while his wife was sentenced to four months and two weeks' imprisonment, suspended for a year.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: Amy Hind, a former Tory party employee who was working as an NHS business support manager, was also sentenced to six months' imprisonment, suspended for a year, after previously pleading guilty to cheating on the date of the election.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: Judge Tony Baumgartner, sentencing the three of them, said their conduct "risked undermining" the confidence the public has in the Conservative Party "as an institution", "undermining trust in the democratic process" and the "integrity of the gambling system".
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: The trio were among several people charged with betting offences by the Gambling Commission.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: The trials of other defendants will take place next year and in 2028.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: Former Conservative MP Craig Williams, who was Sunak's closest parliamentary aide at the time, pleaded guilty in June and will be sentenced at a later date.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: Sunak's decision to call a general election for July 2024 was a surprise to many, including several Conservative MPs, who were expecting an autumn date.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: The court heard that Sunak held a private Downing Street meeting on 10 March of that year to discuss possible dates.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: Neither Lee nor his wife attended the meeting, but the couple began betting online on the election being held in July or between July and September, the court heard.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: Baumgartner described Anthony Lee as a "central figure" in the preparation of the general election, who sat at a group of desks within Tory HQ known as the "God Pod".
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: Representing Lee, barrister Richard Pratt said his client did not concretely know the working date of the election, saying it "still represented a gamble from his point of view".
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: The barrister told the court: "It was always possible the prime minister could change his mind." Pratt said there "wasn't any direct manipulation" by the defendant.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: Laura Lee worked for the Tories as their "head of international" and had been selected as the party candidate for Bristol North West for the election.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: Baumgartner said she had no involvement in the election planning and her access to information "came predominantly" from her husband.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: The court heard Hind's husband Anthony worked as a deputy digital director for the Conservatives but did not place any bets himself.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: Baumgartner said Hind's husband "was party to emails relating to the forthcoming general election and was one potential source of your inside information".
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: The judge later said "someone else who worked within the heart of CCHQ" could have given her the "highly confidential" information.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: The court heard Hind placed four bets and made three further unsuccessful attempts to place bets.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: The unsuccessful attempts were for £767, £700 and £750.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: Baumgartner described them all as having expressed remorse for their actions.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: The trio are now subject to a 12-month prohibited activity requirement, banning them from accessing or using online gambling websites or applications.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: Anthony Lee was ordered to complete 100 hours of unpaid work and pay more than £6,600 in compensation to a betting company, while Laura Lee must carry out 40 hours of unpaid work and pay £4,265.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: Hind was ordered to complete 50 hours of unpaid work.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: Katharine Diamond, General Counsel of regulators the Gambling Commission, reacted to the sentencing of the trio by saying "justice has been served".
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: She described the case as "a first of its kind" and said it demonstrated the commission's "commitment to protecting the integrity of betting markets".

sentences.text: Andy Burnham said military aircraft will be used to tackle wildfires as he tries to ensure the UK is "on the front foot" following a summer of devastating blazes.
sentences.article_title: Military aircraft to help get UK 'on front foot' to fight wildfires, Burnham says

sentences.text: Civilian fire services in all four nations will be able to request the support of the Royal Air Force's Chinook helicopters and A400M planes to fight wildfires on tough terrain such as remote moorland and steep hillsides.
sentences.article_title: Military aircraft to help get UK 'on front foot' to fight wildfires, Burnham says

sentences.text: As he hosted the UK's first summit on wildfires, the prime minister outlined initial steps to "improve our response" after the country "lived through a summer that we've never seen before".
sentences.article_title: Military aircraft to help get UK 'on front foot' to fight wildfires, Burnham says

sentences.text: Burnham said this also includes better equipment for firefighters and improved land management to stop fires from spreading.
sentences.article_title: Military aircraft to help get UK 'on front foot' to fight wildfires, Burnham says

sentences.text: After a record-breaking summer, the government's "wildfire resilience summit" in Liverpool on Friday discussed how to prevent, respond to and recover from such blazes.

sentences.text: There have been 1,350 wildfires in England and Wales this year, an all-time high and up by more than 300 on last year and more than 1,000 on 2024, according to figures from the National Fire Chiefs Council .
sentences.article_title: Military aircraft to help get UK 'on front foot' to fight wildfires, Burnham says

sentences.text: Records for the number of reported wildfires were also broken in 2022 and 2025 - but the UK's Climate Change Committee has warned the risk will rise in the coming decades.

sentences.article_title: Military aircraft to help get UK 'on front foot' to fight wildfires, Burnham says

sentences.text: It is lighter than current firefighting equipment which is designed for fires in buildings and not meant to be worn for a long time, the government added.
sentences.article_title: Military aircraft to help get UK 'on front foot' to fight wildfires, Burnham says

sentences.text: Ministers are also pledging a £25m scheme from April 2027 to April 2029 to restore dried-out peatlands in England so they are natural firebreaks, and financial support for farmers to fireproof their land such as by digging ponds.

sentences.text: "The government will also look at tougher local restrictions or product bans to stop people starting fires when the risk is high," a briefing ahead of the summit said, following a temporary ban on disposable BBQs .

sentences.text: He said: "I think too often in the past we've been playing catch up, and today is trying about trying to get on the front foot and recognise that the summer we've just had is likely to be a more regular situation going forward.

Burnham earlier told reporters that fire and rescue services were "stretched" this summer and firefighters had worked in "extremely difficult conditions" before committing to providing better equipment.

sentences.text: Do you have three days' worth of food and water in your home?
sentences.article_title: Why should I stockpile and what will I need?

sentences.text: That is what the government has told all of us to have on hand to get through a national emergency, as well as some other basic items.
sentences.article_title: Why should I stockpile and what will I need?

sentences.text: Its "Be Ready" campaign warns that severe weather and cyber attacks could disrupt essential services, and British households need to make sure they have what they need to get through a rocky few days.
sentences.article_title: Why should I stockpile and what will I need?

sentences.text: On Friday, Prime Minister Andy Burnham said unexpected events "seem to becoming more common" and everyone should have "those supplies in the house to get you through those moments".
sentences.article_title: Why should I stockpile and what will I need?

sentences.text: As one expert warns the UK is "light years" behind our neighbours when it comes to preparing for major disruption, we've drilled down into what you need and why.
sentences.article_title: Why should I stockpile and what will I need?

sentences.text: The government recommends having enough supplies in the kitchen to last three days, including bottled water and non-perishable foods.
sentences.article_title: Why should I stockpile and what will I need?

sentences.text: Wet wipes, a torch and cash are also recommended - you can scroll through below to see the full list.
sentences.article_title: Why should I stockpile and what will I need?

sentences.text: Disaster planning expert Professor Lucy Easthope said the goal of asking household to prepare is to make it easier for emergency service to cope in the event of a national emergency.
sentences.article_title: Why should I stockpile and what will I need?

sentences.text: For example, the government says people who need medication should have an extra supply just in case.
sentences.article_title: Why should I stockpile and what will I need?

sentences.text: Prof Easthope says: "If people have got their heart pills for an extra 48 hours, it stops [response crews] from having to immediately find an emergency pharmacist." While the latest government campaign only launched on Thursday, some people are well ahead of the game.
sentences.article_title: Why should I stockpile and what will I need?

sentences.text: Speaking to Radio 5 Live, Bridgette Clamp, who lives in near Penzance in Cornwall, said she has stocked up on "lots of tinned goods" as well as "flour, yeast and everything to bake bread".
sentences.article_title: Why should I stockpile and what will I need?

sentences.text: "We're rocking and rolling," she says.
sentences.article_title: Why should I stockpile and what will I need?

sentences.text: Bridgette says she also bought generators and water pumps following Storm Goretti earlier this year One woman, who spoke to 5 Live anonymously, said she bought "loads and loads" of emergency food - but ended up eating it before it was strictly necessary.
sentences.article_title: Why should I stockpile and what will I need?

sentences.text: Like others, she wondered if the government was "scaremongering", adding: "I don't know but I've certainly bought into it." Rob, who lives off-grid in north Wales, told the programme he has stocked up on so many supplies he "wouldn't even notice" if a disaster struck.
sentences.article_title: Why should I stockpile and what will I need?

sentences.text: But he said he still felt there was "a bit of scaremongering" going on and wondered if he would ever need it all.
sentences.article_title: Why should I stockpile and what will I need?

sentences.text: Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said the advice - which is similar to guidance issued by the previous government - was not triggered by any "particular piece of intelligence", but rather about improving "national resilience" more generally.
sentences.article_title: Why should I stockpile and what will I need?

sentences.text: The government's announcement focused on extreme weather events , which are becoming more frequent because of man-made climate change - but Streeting also referred to the threat of "increasingly sophisticated cyber-attacks" on businesses, and supply chain disruption caused by "hostile state actors or terrorists".
sentences.article_title: Why should I stockpile and what will I need?

sentences.text: Prof Easthope said she has been lobbying the government to launch this sort of campaign for "about 16 years".
sentences.article_title: Why should I stockpile and what will I need?

sentences.text: She said successive governments have been hesitant of "putting out information that might cause tension" - and speculated that this advice may have been "rushed" out ahead of Storm Austen hitting the UK.
sentences.article_title: Why should I stockpile and what will I need?

sentences.text: Expert Prof Lucy Easthope says the UK is playing "massive catch up" to other nations in disaster preparedness While many of us will already have a stash of tinned food in the cupboards, fewer homes are likely to have a store of bottled water.
sentences.article_title: Why should I stockpile and what will I need?

sentences.text: Paul from Torquay, Devon, said to Radio 5 Live: "Who on earth carries three day supply of water?" He added: "I think they've made it our responsibility, rather than their responsibility." Prof Easthope described the UK as "light years" behind neighbouring countries when it comes to preparedness.
sentences.article_title: Why should I stockpile and what will I need?

sentences.text: "Countries like Scandinavia, Denmark, Sweden, Norway, they've been good at this for years," she said.
sentences.article_title: Why should I stockpile and what will I need?

sentences.text: France advises people to store 72-hours' worth of food, while the German government says homes should have enough supplies to last for a 10-day period.
sentences.article_title: Why should I stockpile and what will I need?

sentences.text: "This is one area where I'm very comfortable saying we are playing massive catch-up," added Easthope.
sentences.article_title: Why should I stockpile and what will I need?

sentences.text: Awareness campaigns such as "think 72 hours" make a big difference in the US, Australia and "all around Europe", she said.
sentences.article_title: Why should I stockpile and what will I need?

sentences.text: However, in the UK, she said disaster messaging often gets parodied, or governments are accused of "panic-mongering".
sentences.article_title: Why should I stockpile and what will I need?

sentences.text: "We have seen the pendulum shift" in recent years, she adds, saying that "we are now seeing people recognise this" as an issue that needs tackling.
sentences.article_title: Why should I stockpile and what will I need?

sentences.text: The announcement comes after talks had been taking place with the government over the past month, following the vote in favour of strike action by British Medical Association members in July.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: Consultants – the most senior doctors in hospitals – were given a 3.5% pay increase this year.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: But the BMA argues pay has fallen by a quarter over the past 17 years, once inflation is taken into account.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: The union also wants a reduction in the standard working week, from 40 to 35 hours, and higher pay for out-of-hours work, alongside changes to pensions, including greater flexibility over when they can be taken.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: In a joint statement, BMA consultants committee co-chairs Dr Helen Neary and Dr Shanu Datta, said they had tried to negotiate with the government in "good faith", but "time-and-time again ministers have kicked the can down the road".

sentences.text: "Unfortunately, that road has now run out, and we have been forced to announce strikes.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: "Consultants take their responsibilities incredibly seriously, and striking does not come naturally, but we are hearing loud and clear from the profession that they have had enough." Average earnings for consultants top £150,000 a year.

sentences.text: Basic pay starts at £113,500, with the most experienced getting £150,500.

sentences.text: But many earn tens of thousands in extra payments and awards.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: In the strike ballot, 76% of consultants who took part voted in favour of strike action, with just over half of eligible BMA members taking part.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: The government says this represents only around one in five consultants employed by the NHS in England voting for strike action, as nearly half are not BMA members.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: Health Secretary Yvette Cooper said the government had been in "constructive discussions" with the BMA so it was "disappointing" the strike dates had been announced.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: She said taking strike action would be "irresponsible" and "place the health service under even greater pressure".

sentences.text: A clinical trial has been launched in the UK which scientists hope could cut years from the search for new treatments for Alzheimer's disease.

sentences.text: "We have Alzheimer's in the family," she told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: "But I was determined that it wasn't going to define me." Angela said she felt empowered joining the trial because "at least you are doing something".
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: "Instead of just sitting there, you're standing up and saying, I will fight back." Alzheimer's is the most common type of dementia, affecting around 600,000 people in the UK.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: Prime Minister Andy Burnham, whose father died from Alzheimer's last month, said he knew how it felt to lose a loved one to dementia, and had seen first-hand the devastating impact of the disease on families.

sentences.text: "That's why I'm proud to see this trial being launched in the UK, so that cutting-edge treatments can reach patients here as soon as possible," he said.

sentences.text: The AD-SMART study is what's known as a multi-arm, multi-stage platform trial where several treatments are tested simultaneously, with the results compared with one group of participants taking a placebo or dummy.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: This means those involved have a higher likelihood of getting an active treatment than in a traditional trial.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: If any drug isn't showing benefit it can be dropped quickly and a new treatment added in its place - the approach has been used successfully in cancer and motor neurone disease.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: "For too long, Alzheimer's research has moved at the pace of one drug, one trial, one answer - sometimes taking a decade or more before we know if we've found something that works," he told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: "We are applying advances from cancer and other conditions to accelerate testing of treatments for people with Alzheimer's disease." For the drugs to be successful, the study has to show that they have beneficial effects on thinking and the ability to carry out everyday activities.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: "That's what patients and their carers care about," said Prof Malhotra.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study
