sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: Franklin was a British chemist and crystallographer, whose X-ray diffraction work helped discover the structure of DNA Rosalind Franklin is the only female scientist named in GCSE and National 5 science exam specifications in the UK, according to new research.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: A Cambridge study found that of the 86 scientists named by UK exam boards, the English chemist, whose work in the 1950s helped reveal the structure of DNA, was the only woman.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Exam specifications set out the skills and knowledge students are expected to have gained by the end of their course and how they will be assessed.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Academics from the University of Cambridge, along with institutions in the US and Australia, examined how many women were mentioned in specifications for biology, chemistry, physics, environmental science, geology and astronomy.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Their work, published in the British Educational Research Journal, looked at six exam boards in the UK: At Key Stage 4 and equivalent, including GCSEs and National 5s in Scotland, Franklin was the only woman among the 86 scientists mentioned.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: She was also one of three women mentioned at Key Stage 5 and equivalent - including A-levels, AS-levels, National Highers and National Advanced Highers - out of a total of 181 scientists.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Marie Tharp, an American cartographer who created the first map of the floor of the Atlantic ocean in the 1950s, and Inge Lehmann, a Danish seismologist who discovered the existence of the Earth's inner core in the 1930s, both feature in the Cambridge OCR's A-­level Geology.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Franklin, who was named in Cambridge OCR's GCSE Biology and Scottish Highers Biology, produced a famous DNA image known as Photograph 51.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Cambridge scientists Francis Crick and James Watson used the image to work out the following year that DNA has a double-helix structure.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Watson, Crick and Franklin's colleague Maurice Wilkins received the 1962 Nobel Prize for the discovery.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Franklin had died four years earlier.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Academics who wrote the paper found that "several major scientific breakthroughs" in specifications were made by women, but they were not explicitly mentioned.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: The paper said: "Many of the scientific discoveries and explanations were developed in the 1800s and early 1900s, a period when scientific and mathematical practice was largely, but not solely, dominated by men.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: "Our findings confirm that the UK science specifications reflect this historical imbalance: although women made significant contributions to major scientific breakthroughs, this fact is rarely acknowledged." The academics recommended that Franklin should be included "in all specifications when teaching DNA structure".
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: They also said specifications should refer to Marie Curie, who discovered radium and polonium and coined the term radioactivity, and nuclear physicist Lise Meitner, who discovered nuclear fission, among others.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Education Secretary Lucy Powell says the government will "update and strengthen" Holocaust education within schools after a major review highlighted the "shocking scale" of antisemitism in British society.

sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: "I do really feel it is a generational moment to educate this generation and the next – that is the job of education – to understand what antisemitism is in the modern world." sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: As temperatures exceed 30C (86F) in some parts of the UK this week, the last thing people want to do is turn on the oven.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Not only can cooking in hot weather feel like a chore, but many of us find ourselves feeling less hungry altogether.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So when the heat gets too much, should we consider changing our diet?
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Here are three things to think about next time you're hot and hungry.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Cooking chicken in an air fryer uses less than half the energy of a conventional oven "There's no need for more protein in a heatwave," says Aisling Daly, senior lecturer in nutrition at Oxford Brookes University.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But if you fancy it, some of the most common proteins will need cooking (like meat, chicken and fish) and that can be off-putting in the heat.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even an outdoor BBQ can be too hot to handle.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Cooking a chicken leg in the worktop device uses less than half the energy of a conventional oven, according to Radio 4's Sliced Bread .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: And because they are smaller and speedier, they also pump less heat into your kitchen.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But experts say don't forget about your slightly less fashionable slow cooker - likely buried in the back of your cupboard.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even though they run for longer, they're typically more energy efficient and release even less heat than the air fryer.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: The reality, though, is that simply by eating and digesting protein, our bodies produce more heat than other food groups.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: That's due to the energy needed by the stomach, intestines and liver to break down and absorb these complex molecules.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So that steak you crave will only bring you out in a sweat.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But you can also get your protein from lentils, nuts, milk, tofu and cheese too.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: To reduce body heat while still getting your protein fix, Dr Daly recommends focusing on things like bean salads, eggs, pre-cooked meats and plenty of Greek yoghurt (frozen too).
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Making a smoothie by blending up fruit, veg and yogurt (while adding in peanut butter for protein) can provide a balanced, nutritious meal in an easy way.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: And it might also be time to turn to some lighter fish, such as tuna, salmon or prawns.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: When it's hot, we lose water when we sweat, so we need to replace it or we become dehydrated.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Six to eight glasses of fluid a day is normally recommended by the NHS, , external and in a heatwave you could need a lot more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: "There is no single amount that suits everyone, because how much fluid your body needs depends on lots of factors like your age, body size, activity levels and health status," says Dr Charlotte Mills, food and nutrition scientist at the University of Reading.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: World Cup footballers aren't the only ones who benefit from hydration breaks: other athletes and pregnant and breastfeeding women are among those who need to drink more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But rehydrating doesn't just mean refilling your water bottle every couple of hours.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: "We need to eat our water as well as drink it," says Dr Daly, "80-90% of fruit and vegetables are full of water." Cucumber, tomatoes, lettuce, celery, watermelon and strawberries all have very high water content, above 90%.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Apples, carrots, cooked broccoli and pears contain 80% to 89% water, as do oranges, grapes and pineapple.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: In comparison, boiled eggs are 75% water , external , with digestive biscuits only 2.8% water , external .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even a cheese and tomato pizza is 38% water, with takeaway chips containing as much as 51%.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: If your mouth has dried up just reading this, try some of these water-rich recipes .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: A useful way to check if you're hydrated is to check the colour of your urine.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Pale yellow is what you're after.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: If it's orangey or dark brown, that's a sign that your kidneys - which filter waste products and produce urine - are holding onto water because there isn't enough in the body.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: That means you're dehydrated and need to drink more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Warm or room-temperature drinks are just as good as cold ones for cooling you down We know some people love a cuppa, even when it's sweltering, and that actually makes scientific sense.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Warm or room-temperature drinks are just as good as cold ones for cooling you down, says Dr Daly.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Research suggests your body sweats more quickly to get rid of the excess heat after a hot drink.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: After a cold drink, your body sweats more slowly.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Your body is trying to keep your core temperature steady at about 37 degrees celsius.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So hot tea won't necessarily help you cool down more quickly - the key thing is to stay hydrated no matter the temperature of the liquid.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: You don't need to shun your favourite coffee either just because it's hot - although too much caffeine can make the body produce more urine, and leave you dehydrated.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: For matcha fans, the drink contains more caffeine than a cup of tea but less than a regular coffee.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Dr Daly says one or two coffees a day should make little difference to your hydration levels - but five or six will start to have an effect.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Bear in mind that drinking alcohol also dehydrates.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: You could structure your day differently too, and take a southern European approach to eating.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Have an early breakfast, an afternoon siesta while it's very hot and then a late dinner.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: WhatsApp is introducing new parental controls for teenagers, as tech companies continue to come under pressure to provide more age-appropriate experiences for children.

sentences.text: The social messaging app's new tools will give parents a range of options, such as being told when their child joins or leaves a group.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: It will also let them decide on privacy settings for their account.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: In a blog post, WhatsApp, clarified parents would not be given the power to see the messages their teen is sending and receiving, which along with calls would stay private and protected by end-to-end encryption.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: And it said the controls were optional, which social media analyst Matt Navarra called an "obvious weakness".
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: He said the move was "fairly convenient" for Meta, which owns WhatsApp, because it reduced the company's reliance on age verification by putting some responsibility on parents and teenagers.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: "Meta is trying to show regulators we have a child safety system, we have parental controls and we're rolling it out across our platforms," he said.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: "I think the big unanswered question is whether enough families will actually use it." The minimum age to use WhatsApp is 13 in the UK, although it is higher in some countries.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: According to the firm, parents will be able to adjust or switch off the controls at any time.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: The settings will be "straightforward to set up" using a Pin set by a parent, which teens will need if they want to switch off the controls.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: Some of the new privacy tools include selecting who can see a child's profile photo and who can add them to groups.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: Parents can also choose how their teenager uses Channels, which allows organisations and public figures to send out content.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: And they will have the option of choosing between the default 13+ setting for Meta AI, the app's optional built-in AI assistant, or a stricter "Limited Content" option.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: "All of these controls are being designed to support open conversations about how to use WhatsApp between parents and teens, while keeping everyone's personal messages private," the company said.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: The changes come as pressure mounts on tech companies from governments and regulators to change the way they operate in order to better protect children using their platforms.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: In June, the government announced it plans to ban under-16s from social media platforms, with the restrictions expected to come into force in March 2027.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: It said "highly effective age assurance" measures would be used to check the age of those using social media.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: WhatsApp is currently excluded from the ban because the government considers it a messaging service.

sentences.text: The Artemis III mission will not head to the Moon.

sentences.text: Meta chief executive Mark Zuckerberg Meta has agreed to a new deal with chief executive Mark Zuckerberg to prevent him from leaving California over a proposed state tax on billionaires.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: The agreement gives Zuckerberg, whose wealth is estimated to exceed $200bn (£149bn), even more shares in Meta to make up for the fraction of his fortune he may lose if the tax wins voter approval in November.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: The measure would impose a one-time 5% tax on residents with a net worth of more than $1bn.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: It would likely see the Facebook co-founder pay around $10bn in additional state taxes.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: He secured the deal with a special committee of Meta after "robust" and "at several points, contentious" negotiations, according to a Wednesday financial disclosure.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: California is home to most of the US's technology giants and there are around 225 billionaires who reside in the state, according to the Americans for Tax Fairness campaign group.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: The wealth of such people, including Zuckerberg, has ballooned in recent years.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: Meanwhile, his estimated effective tax rate in California was less than 1% , external each year.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: Nevertheless, Zuckerberg told Meta's board last month that he was thinking of moving his primary residence out of California, and even selling his property in the state.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: His main homes in Californa are in Palo Alto and Lake Tahoe.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: Such a move "would be public and inevitably noted and commented upon by company employees", Zuckerberg told the board.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: It would also "raise questions for management of the company going forward", he claimed.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: In response, Meta decided to create more shares of stock in the company in order to give Zuckerberg a way to essentially make up any wealth he may lose through the tax proposal.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: Through what's known as a stock split announced by the company on Wednesday , Meta created an entirely new type of stock and gave one new share to each existing shareholder.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: Zuckerberg is one of the company's largest shareholders and famously controls the company through the design of his holdings.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: Through the deal, he will receive more stock, more often, and also be able to sell it on a quarterly basis, according to the company's financial filing.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: The shares will not change his level control over Meta, but they will allow him to cash in more easily on the company's value.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: The deal appears to be effective even if the one-time tax in California does not pass, and will go on for eight years - as long as Zuckerberg remains a resident of California.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: After a surge in hiring at Meta during the pandemic, a whistleblower scandal that led to renewed focus on child safety, and a refocus within the company to building out the "metaverse," which included renaming the company Meta from Facebook, the company began mass layoffs and restructuring.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: Layoffs have continued into this year.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: The company's headcount is down 15% from a year ago, meaning it has shed at least 10,000 workers.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: Today, the company has moved away from the "metaverse," or virtual platforms, and is more focused on artificial intelligence products and related tools.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: With Zuckerberg leading the company's efforts to catch up in the AI race, Meta's board said it sees a future of "tremendous market opportunity" for the company.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: Major tech companies are set to spend an estimated $1 trillion , external this year alone developing AI and the costly infrastructure around it, like data centres .
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: Meta said on Wednesday it planned to spend as much as $145bn this year on AI projects.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: The company has increased the amount it expects to spend on AI each financial quarter so far this year.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: It is spending so much on the technology that it posted negative cash flow for the first time since the company went public 14 years ago.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: Cash flow represents the money a company retains after paying for operations and investments, meaning Meta is now spending more money than it is bringing in.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: And the company intends to spend even more in the year ahead.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: Susan Li, Meta's chief financial officer, said on Wednesday that another benefit of the stock split would be to give the company more ways to finance future spending on AI work.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: The degree of the company's spending on AI, without an clear new revenue stream coming from it, appeared to spook investors on Thursday.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: Meta's shares fell more than 7%, wiping more than $100bn off of the company's market capitalisation, a key metric used worldwide to measure the value of a publicly-traded company.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: Ash Dykes' latest challenge involves six back-to-back feats of extreme endurance An adventurer has completed the first leg of his latest challenge after losing contact with his UK team for almost 24 hours.
sentences.article_title: Adventurer completes 400-mile expedition after losing contact with team

sentences.text: Ash Dykes, 35, from Old Colwyn, Conwy, holds five world records but his most recent quest was the first of six back-to-back expeditions he will take on in extreme environments.
sentences.article_title: Adventurer completes 400-mile expedition after losing contact with team

sentences.text: Dykes encountered elephants, gorillas and was chased by "killer" bees as he rowed more than 434 miles (700 km) along rivers in the Congo Basin, central Africa.
sentences.article_title: Adventurer completes 400-mile expedition after losing contact with team

sentences.text: Towards the end of the journey, Dykes' portable satellite kit lost power.
sentences.article_title: Adventurer completes 400-mile expedition after losing contact with team

sentences.text: He said: "My parents and fiancée were worrying but as soon as I had a bit of signal I made sure I got in touch".
sentences.article_title: Adventurer completes 400-mile expedition after losing contact with team

sentences.text: This video can not be played Ash says the world is not ready for a "truly live expedition" In his latest Project 6 challenge, Dykes will attempt six expeditions in very different locations.
sentences.article_title: Adventurer completes 400-mile expedition after losing contact with team

sentences.text: He has previously walked 4,000-miles (6,437km) along the length of China's Yangtze River in 2019 and kayaked the length of the Coppename river in Suriname from source to sea in 37 days On "going missing", Dykes said his "power bank just shut down".
sentences.article_title: Adventurer completes 400-mile expedition after losing contact with team

sentences.text: "We were underneath the jungle canopy, because we were staying with a small community, and then it took me about 20 hours before I could get out the first message," he said.
sentences.article_title: Adventurer completes 400-mile expedition after losing contact with team

sentences.text: As the adventurer is sharing expeditions "live", he said he had learned lessons from the experience going forward.
sentences.article_title: Adventurer completes 400-mile expedition after losing contact with team

sentences.text: He said: "I don't think the world's ready for a truly live expedition so I've learned from that...
sentences.article_title: Adventurer completes 400-mile expedition after losing contact with team

sentences.text: "If I lose contact again with the team, we have to keep it within the team because I do know that that hit alarms and a lot of people were stressed and panicked.
sentences.article_title: Adventurer completes 400-mile expedition after losing contact with team

sentences.text: He said: "We took the warnings seriously.
sentences.article_title: Adventurer completes 400-mile expedition after losing contact with team

sentences.text: Experience means listening to local advice, reading the conditions and making the decisions that get your team through safely." For the explorer, the main highlight was spending time with the Baka tribe, a semi-nomadic indigenous ethnic group.
sentences.article_title: Adventurer completes 400-mile expedition after losing contact with team

sentences.text: They demonstrated their hunting prowess which involves trapping animals in netting set up around the jungle.
sentences.article_title: Adventurer completes 400-mile expedition after losing contact with team

sentences.text: "They were amazing, they took us under their wings, they showed us how they survive, how they hunt, how they gather," Dykes said.
sentences.article_title: Adventurer completes 400-mile expedition after losing contact with team

sentences.text: "They took us to an area where we saw a group of gorillas within Sanga National Park.
sentences.article_title: Adventurer completes 400-mile expedition after losing contact with team

sentences.text: I was about five metres away from silverback." Ash Dykes was waved off on his journey by local people Dykes was joined on his trek by local guide Obed Temba Tuyumvire as well as videographer Will Perez, who has been helping chart the journey with regular social media posts.
sentences.article_title: Adventurer completes 400-mile expedition after losing contact with team

sentences.text: His popularity on TikTok has soared following his latest adventure.
sentences.article_title: Adventurer completes 400-mile expedition after losing contact with team

sentences.text: Dykes said: "It felt like the world was on the river with us." But he added some followers were disappointed in the lack of drama.
sentences.article_title: Adventurer completes 400-mile expedition after losing contact with team

sentences.text: "Everyone wanted that excitement, that danger, but if something was to happen, I'd be criticised: 'this is dangerous'.
sentences.article_title: Adventurer completes 400-mile expedition after losing contact with team

sentences.text: "Now that I've made it unscathed, everyone's like: 'It's easy, there were no crocs'.
sentences.article_title: Adventurer completes 400-mile expedition after losing contact with team

sentences.text: "So there's no true winning when you go that viral." He said he lost 11lbs (5kg) during the trip, as he was relying mostly on ration packs of food.
sentences.article_title: Adventurer completes 400-mile expedition after losing contact with team

sentences.text: In a social media post to mark the end of the first stage of Project 6, Dykes said: "It's been a lot.
sentences.article_title: Adventurer completes 400-mile expedition after losing contact with team

sentences.text: We've faced ups and downs - seen some crazy wildlife, but more importantly we've survived." Dykes said he would reveal the second stage of Project 6 next week, and hinted it would be somewhere "a lot colder" than the Congo Basin.

sentences.text: Kaual Patel took over the shop from his father and uncle 20 years ago A corner shop owner from south London has been painted by a royal portraitist in a project to recognise the impact of independent businesses in their local communities.
sentences.article_title: Shopkeeper immortalised by royal portrait artist

sentences.text: Artist Nick Bashall, who painted Princess Anne, has depicted Kaual Patel, owner of Torridon Convenience Store in Catford.
sentences.article_title: Shopkeeper immortalised by royal portrait artist

sentences.text: The work will be revealed to the public in a new exhibition, Local Royalty, alongside paintings by other royal artists of pub, cafe and takeaway owners.
sentences.article_title: Shopkeeper immortalised by royal portrait artist

sentences.text: The event was inspired by research that indicated nearly 80% of the public believed independent businesses such as corner shops are underappreciated.
sentences.article_title: Shopkeeper immortalised by royal portrait artist

sentences.text: The artist Nick Bashall said watching customers wondering what was going on "was great fun" The exhibition depicts Patel alongside three other small business owners who have been immortalised in a manner historically reserved for royalty, titans of industry and stars of stage and screen.
sentences.article_title: Shopkeeper immortalised by royal portrait artist

sentences.text: He took over the shop from his father and uncle and has spent the past two decades creating a hub for the local community and championing local producers.
sentences.article_title: Shopkeeper immortalised by royal portrait artist

sentences.text: "The days I spent being painted by Nick, live in the shop, were unforgettable, but what made it truly special was seeing it through the eyes of my customers," said Patel.
sentences.article_title: Shopkeeper immortalised by royal portrait artist

sentences.text: Patel said: "This simply doesn't happen to an everyday shopkeeper" "This wasn't created behind closed doors in a studio.
sentences.article_title: Shopkeeper immortalised by royal portrait artist

sentences.text: It happened right here, in the store, surrounded by the people who make our community so special.
sentences.article_title: Shopkeeper immortalised by royal portrait artist

sentences.text: Seeing their expressions, hearing their reactions and watching the portrait come to life alongside them created memories I'll never forget.
sentences.article_title: Shopkeeper immortalised by royal portrait artist

sentences.text: "This simply doesn't happen to an everyday shopkeeper." Bashall said: "I stood at my easel and painted Kaual and the entire background on the spot, with people milling around us.
sentences.article_title: Shopkeeper immortalised by royal portrait artist

sentences.text: "It was great fun watching his customers' faces as they came in, clearly wondering what was going on, but also intrigued by it all." The exhibition, sponsored by Coca-Cola GB, will be open to the public from 28 October to 2 November at the Saatchi Gallery in London.
sentences.article_title: Shopkeeper immortalised by royal portrait artist

sentences.text: African diaspora is finding new audiences in a city celebrated for its musical heritage A new sound is taking Bristol's dancefloors by storm.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Driven by rolling log drums, syncopated rhythms and infectious melodies, amapiano and other electronic sounds from across the African diaspora are finding new audiences in a city celebrated for its musical heritage.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Behind these parties is a new generation of black promoters passionate about creating spaces where black people can hear their music, celebrate their cultures and feel like they belong.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: But for some, building these spaces has also meant confronting the familiar challenge of finding spaces where black music and the communities around it are welcomed and not feared.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Unkle Mykel started hosting events to connect to different cultures Bristol-based promoter Unkle Mykel's journey into events began in his own back garden after he moved to Bristol in 2017.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: What started as garden barbecues gradually grew into a way of bringing people together, particularly members of Bristol's black, Asian and minority ethnic communities.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "It's about celebrating our cultures, bringing people into that fold and connecting," says the 32-year-old, who hosts Bristol Barbecue Family and The Aux Social.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Originally from Kenya, Mykel moved to the UK in 2005.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Since then, he has witnessed changes in the visibility of African music.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "There was no Afrobeats on the airwaves," he laughs, recalling his early years in the country, when he says Caribbean reggae, dancehall and soca were more prominent in the musical landscape he encountered.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Now, he sees the growing popularity of genres such as amapiano - a popular South African house music subgenre - as an opportunity to broaden the scene.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "We don't need to pretend to be nobody else, we're just us.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: It just took a while to get there." DJ and promoter Khiah Lou runs amapiano event called Khaya Nights For 30-year-old DJ and promoter Khiah Lou, representation, she says, is central to her work.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Last year she launched Khaya Nights, an event dedicated to amapiano and other African Caribbean electronic dance music.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Having performed internationally, she had seen how other cities had developed a wider range of events celebrating these sounds.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Bristol, she felt, was lagging behind.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Rather than wait for the scene to develop, Khiah decided to help build it herself.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "If we don't do it, who else is going to do it?" she says.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "Young black people are starting to make a way for themselves because I don't think we have a choice." Khiah says these nights provide a place where people can connect with their identities and see their cultures reflected in the city around them.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "At first it seems like it's just a party, but it's so much more than that," she says.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "It's really important for your own self-identity.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: If your community doesn't have events, where do you feel you can go?" "At first it seems like just a party, but it's so much more than that,' says Khiah Tazmin Samuels, who DJs as Azumei, shares those concerns about representation.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: As part of Rushtown, a black-led music collective, Tazmin wants to champion sounds and subcultures from across Africa, Latin America and the Caribbean.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "My main motivation for getting together with people and starting Rushtown came from seeing the lack of representation of black music that black people are currently listening to within the city," says Tazmin.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: She sees encouraging signs, with more black music-focused brands emerging in Bristol.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: But she believes the wider music industry has yet to recognise the value of what these promoters are building.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Tazmin says the wider music industry must recognise the value of black promoters But creating these spaces is not always straightforward.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Khiah says she has struggled to find venues willing to host nights aimed at black audiences.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Although she considers Bristol an inclusive city, her experience as a promoter has revealed a different side of its nightlife.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "I've had some venue owners straight up tell me they're worried about having a black event," she says.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "I feel like black crowds are kind of met with fear, and that's really disheartening." Mykel describes similar tensions, saying that some venues are enthusiastic about hosting his events, only to face objections from people in the surrounding community.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: The Bamboo Club opened in 1966 as a social hub for Bristol's Caribbean community The young promoters' experiences echo a much longer history of black Bristolians having to create their own spaces for music and social life.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Many black people were turned away from existing clubs and bars in Bristol during the 1960s, which led to the creation of  "blues parties", un-licensed house parties where people danced to genres such as ska, reggae and rocksteady.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: In 1966, Tony Bullimore and his Jamaican-born wife Lalel, opened the Bamboo Club, which served as a cultural lifeline for the city's Caribbean community.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Glen Crooks, 70, who used to perform at the Bamboo Club when he was younger, remembers "sneaking in" with his friends when they were young.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "It was the only place that we could have," he recalls.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "Especially all the Caribbean people could go and really have a good time." Rushtown aims to champion a variety of music genres from the African diaspora Marti Burgess, who has been a co-owner of the nightclub Lakota since 1994, says although attitudes have changed over the years, some prejudices remain.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "There is a long history of treating a predominantly black audience as a concern, rather than recognising the audience, creativity and business that a promoter is bringing," she says.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "They should not have to keep proving that black audiences are welcome or commercially worthwhile." Growing up, Marti was surrounded by music.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Her parents went to the blues clubs and attended the Bamboo Club when it hosted artists such as Bob Marley, Desmond Dekker and Johnny Nash.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "It was through listening to the adults' conversations that I came to understand how much those spaces had grown out of exclusion from mainstream venues," she says.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "Latino Fest this summer opened our eyes further to the audiences and musical communities we could welcome," says Marti.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "We want people across the different genres of black music to see Lakota as a venue that is open to them, where they can bring their music and their audiences." Follow BBC Bristol on Facebook , external , X , external and Instagram , external .

sentences.text: Ferrari are one of the six car manufacturers in F1 involved in discussions over the proposed new rules Formula 1's next engine regulations are set to introduce V8 turbo hybrid engines that are simplified and less expensive to make compared to the existing rules.
sentences.article_title: Simpler, cheaper hybrid V8s proposed for next F1 rules

sentences.text: A proposal document sent by governing body the FIA to the six manufacturers in F1 outlines a framework for discussions on engines to be introduced in either 2030 or 2031.
sentences.article_title: Simpler, cheaper hybrid V8s proposed for next F1 rules

sentences.text: Multiple sources within F1 have provided BBC Sport with the details within the document.
sentences.article_title: Simpler, cheaper hybrid V8s proposed for next F1 rules

sentences.text: The plan, which comes after initial discussions with individual engine manufacturers on a one-to-one basis, proposes cheaper, lighter, simpler engines with a more visceral sound.
sentences.article_title: Simpler, cheaper hybrid V8s proposed for next F1 rules

sentences.text: However, the FIA has moved away from its initial proposal to return to naturally aspirated engines.
sentences.article_title: Simpler, cheaper hybrid V8s proposed for next F1 rules

sentences.text: The stated aim of the new rules is to introduce lighter, more responsive cars, increased emphasis on driver skill, relevant technologies, reduced cost, to make it easier for new manufacturers to enter F1 and to continue with the sport's commitment to reducing emissions.
sentences.article_title: Simpler, cheaper hybrid V8s proposed for next F1 rules

sentences.text: This comes after criticism of the new engines introduced this year for their complexity and the way their design and operation has diminished the driving challenge of some of F1's best corners.
sentences.article_title: Simpler, cheaper hybrid V8s proposed for next F1 rules

sentences.text: Will F1 go back to the future with its engines?
sentences.article_title: Simpler, cheaper hybrid V8s proposed for next F1 rules

sentences.text: The engines used in F1 at the moment are 1.6-litre V6 turbos with a power split of 53-47 between the internal combustion engine and electrical components.
sentences.article_title: Simpler, cheaper hybrid V8s proposed for next F1 rules

sentences.text: This will be changed to 60-40 in two steps by 2028.
sentences.article_title: Simpler, cheaper hybrid V8s proposed for next F1 rules

sentences.text: The FIA document proposes a V8 engine with a capacity of between 2-2.3-litres with a smaller turbo running at reduced boost pressure and a less powerful hybrid system.
sentences.article_title: Simpler, cheaper hybrid V8s proposed for next F1 rules

sentences.text: The electrical motor would have a recovery capacity of 200kW compared to the current 350kW.
sentences.article_title: Simpler, cheaper hybrid V8s proposed for next F1 rules

sentences.text: The idea is for 100kW (134bhp) of this to be available at all times, with a further 100kW to be used for a push-to-pass or overtake mode.
sentences.article_title: Simpler, cheaper hybrid V8s proposed for next F1 rules

sentences.text: The rest of the total power output of in the region of 900bhp will be provided by the internal combustion engine.
sentences.article_title: Simpler, cheaper hybrid V8s proposed for next F1 rules

sentences.text: F1 will continue with fully sustainable fuels but with the ambition to make the requirements around them less complex and therefore lower production costs.
sentences.article_title: Simpler, cheaper hybrid V8s proposed for next F1 rules

sentences.text: The aim is to cut a total of 80kg from the overall weight of the cars.
sentences.article_title: Simpler, cheaper hybrid V8s proposed for next F1 rules

sentences.text: The proposal changes the previous stance of the FIA on naturally aspirated engines - president Mohammed Ben Sulayem initially proposed a return of V10s at the start of last year and has more recently been pushing V8s.
sentences.article_title: Simpler, cheaper hybrid V8s proposed for next F1 rules

sentences.text: The addition of the turbo satisfies the need for the engines to be road-relevant, as well as increasing efficiency and requiring less fuel than a pure naturally aspirated engine.
sentences.article_title: Simpler, cheaper hybrid V8s proposed for next F1 rules

sentences.text: The published proposals can be seen as a kind of middle ground between Ben Sulayem's initial stance, the desire of at least some manufacturers to keep turbos and a significant hybrid element, and a recognition that the latest rules were flawed in concept and execution.
sentences.article_title: Simpler, cheaper hybrid V8s proposed for next F1 rules

sentences.text: The new engines will have none of the problems of energy starvation about which drivers have complained this season.
sentences.article_title: Simpler, cheaper hybrid V8s proposed for next F1 rules

sentences.text: Fernando Alonso has called F1 the "battery world championship" and described fast corners as "the charging station for the car", while Max Verstappen has described the new rules  as "Formula E on steroids" and anti-racing.
sentences.article_title: Simpler, cheaper hybrid V8s proposed for next F1 rules

sentences.text: Both have since tempered their criticisms having seen that the sport's bosses have listened to their comments on the engines and made immediate changes to the rules this year as well as started working towards a new direction in the future.
sentences.article_title: Simpler, cheaper hybrid V8s proposed for next F1 rules

sentences.article_title: Simpler, cheaper hybrid V8s proposed for next F1 rules

sentences.text: However, the details around how the rules operate will need discussion.

sentences.article_title: Simpler, cheaper hybrid V8s proposed for next F1 rules

sentences.text: That threat appears to have receded and the process has been marked by a spirit of co-operation, which is expected to continue.

sentences.text: Here is everything you need to know about New Zealand's 2026 general election.
sentences.article_title: New Zealand election 2026: What you need to know

sentences.text: New Zealand holds a general election every three years and uses a Mixed-Member Proportional system or MMP.
sentences.article_title: New Zealand election 2026: What you need to know

sentences.text: Each voter makes two choices - the representative of their constituency in parliament and a political party.
sentences.article_title: New Zealand election 2026: What you need to know

sentences.text: The candidate in a constituency with the most votes wins and becomes an MP.
sentences.article_title: New Zealand election 2026: What you need to know

sentences.text: Political parties on the other hand must win at least 5% of the total party votes to secure a seat in parliament.
sentences.article_title: New Zealand election 2026: What you need to know

sentences.text: The seats are also allocated proportionately - if a party wins 40% of the total party votes, it will get 40% of the seats alloted for parties.
sentences.article_title: New Zealand election 2026: What you need to know

sentences.text: The New Zealand parliament typically has 120 seats - 71 are allocated to constituencies and the remaining 49 are distributed to parties proportionately.
sentences.article_title: New Zealand election 2026: What you need to know

sentences.text: New Zealand elections rarely result in an outright majority and parties forge coalitions to form a government.
sentences.article_title: New Zealand election 2026: What you need to know

sentences.text: New Zealand adopted the MMP in 1996 to address concerns that small parties were being left out of the vote.
sentences.article_title: New Zealand election 2026: What you need to know

sentences.text: The current government is led by Prime Minister Christopher Luxon, whose centre-right National party came to power in 2023 .

sentences.article_title: Hundreds of IDF investigations into killings still have no public outcome, BBC Verify finds

sentences.text: We built an AI search engine to look through those reports for incidents where people may have been injured or killed by Israeli forces, and where the IDF said the report was being investigated, or for example "looked into", "reviewed", "checked" or "examined".
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of IDF investigations into killings still have no public outcome, BBC Verify finds

sentences.text: This identified almost 5,000 reports.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of IDF investigations into killings still have no public outcome, BBC Verify finds

sentences.text: Each one was manually checked by BBC Verify reporters, who excluded any which did not meet the criteria above.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of IDF investigations into killings still have no public outcome, BBC Verify finds

sentences.text: This left 1,343 reports of incidents that the IDF said it was looking into.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of IDF investigations into killings still have no public outcome, BBC Verify finds

sentences.text: Some of these reports described the same incidents.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of IDF investigations into killings still have no public outcome, BBC Verify finds

sentences.text: We built another AI tool to remove these duplicate reports.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of IDF investigations into killings still have no public outcome, BBC Verify finds

sentences.text: It grouped reports into unique incidents based on the publication date, incident date, location, and numbers reported injured or killed.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of IDF investigations into killings still have no public outcome, BBC Verify finds

sentences.text: We then manually checked that each report had been assigned to the correct group, leaving us with 300 unique incidents.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of IDF investigations into killings still have no public outcome, BBC Verify finds

sentences.text: For each of these incidents we then manually checked our records including the incident date, location, and how many people were killed or injured against the original BBC News or Reuters report.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of IDF investigations into killings still have no public outcome, BBC Verify finds

sentences.text: We shared the details of each case with the IDF including the incident date, location, the news report describing the incident, and the IDF's original comment indicating it was looking into the matter.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of IDF investigations into killings still have no public outcome, BBC Verify finds

sentences.text: We asked the IDF for comment and the latest status of each case.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of IDF investigations into killings still have no public outcome, BBC Verify finds

sentences.text: The IDF did not say whether any of these investigations had concluded in response to the BBC's requests.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of IDF investigations into killings still have no public outcome, BBC Verify finds

sentences.text: For each incident we also looked for statements on the IDF's website suggesting that the investigation had been concluded, using two different AI assisted web search engines.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of IDF investigations into killings still have no public outcome, BBC Verify finds

sentences.text: We found evidence that 28 cases were closed based on statements detailing the findings or indicating that no further steps would be taken.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of IDF investigations into killings still have no public outcome, BBC Verify finds

sentences.text: For a further 18 incidents, it was unclear whether the investigation had been concluded.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of IDF investigations into killings still have no public outcome, BBC Verify finds

sentences.text: This included cases where the IDF published initial information about the incident without a clear indication it was closed, and cases where the IDF had characterised some or all of the people killed or injured as combatants, in statements on its own website.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of IDF investigations into killings still have no public outcome, BBC Verify finds

sentences.text: This left us with at least 254 incidents of harm the Israeli military had said it was looking into, for which we did not find a public outcome on the IDF's website.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of IDF investigations into killings still have no public outcome, BBC Verify finds

sentences.text: This was not an exhaustive search, and it is likely that there are more investigations into incidents of harm that were not captured in our search.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of IDF investigations into killings still have no public outcome, BBC Verify finds

sentences.text: Immigration has always been central to Donald Trump's message.
sentences.article_title: Five ways Trump has changed immigration in the US

sentences.text: When he famously stepped onto the golden escalator at Trump Tower to announce his candidacy for his first presidential term in 2015, he accused Mexico of sending drugs and crime north of the border - and it's been a constant rallying cry ever since.
sentences.article_title: Five ways Trump has changed immigration in the US

sentences.text: Some of his first-term ambitions to stem the flow of would-be immigrants were constrained by the courts.
sentences.article_title: Five ways Trump has changed immigration in the US

sentences.text: But restraints have been weaker in his second term, with a more accommodating Supreme Court and tens of billions of additional enforcement money from Congress.
sentences.article_title: Five ways Trump has changed immigration in the US

sentences.text: Who should be allowed to live in the US remains a big issue on the minds of voters in the upcoming midterm elections, which are largely seen as a referendum on the Trump presidency.
sentences.article_title: Five ways Trump has changed immigration in the US

sentences.text: He promised a closed border and mass deportations in his successful 2024 campaign - and few can deny that he's delivered on both.
sentences.article_title: Five ways Trump has changed immigration in the US

sentences.text: But even among those who voted for a tougher stance, there is a concern that the crackdown has gone too far.
sentences.article_title: Five ways Trump has changed immigration in the US

sentences.text: His signature policy has played out in five key ways.
sentences.article_title: Five ways Trump has changed immigration in the US

sentences.text: Crossings exploded during Joe Biden's presidency, with over 4.5 million migrant "encounters" recorded at the southern border in 2023 and 2024 alone, reflecting the massive numbers of people headed north to the US border.
sentences.article_title: Five ways Trump has changed immigration in the US

sentences.text: His administration eventually brought the monthly figures down significantly by restricting asylum claims and removing migrants entering the US illegally without processing.
sentences.article_title: Five ways Trump has changed immigration in the US

sentences.text: When Trump returned to office, that stream of migrants became a trickle.
sentences.article_title: Five ways Trump has changed immigration in the US

sentences.text: Border encounters plummeted.
sentences.article_title: Five ways Trump has changed immigration in the US

sentences.text: By the end of Trump's first year in office, the chaotic scenes that had generated headlines around the globe during the Biden administration had largely gone.
sentences.article_title: Five ways Trump has changed immigration in the US

sentences.text: On a trip to the border city of El Paso, Texas, in November 2025, for example, the BBC found quiet streets where there had previously been makeshift camps housing thousands of migrants granted parole in the US to await immigration proceedings.
sentences.article_title: Five ways Trump has changed immigration in the US

sentences.text: To achieve what he often describes as the "most secure" border in US history, the Trump administration has taken an aggressive, multi-pronged approach.
sentences.article_title: Five ways Trump has changed immigration in the US

sentences.text: That has included effectively freezing asylum applications at the border, ending "catch and release" of detainees into the US, deploying troops to the border and pressuring Mexico to clamp down on the flow of migrants headed north.
sentences.article_title: Five ways Trump has changed immigration in the US

sentences.text: "President Trump promised the American people a secure border, and the data proves he delivered," Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said in a statement on 16 October.
sentences.article_title: Five ways Trump has changed immigration in the US

sentences.text: "The results could not be clearer: strong enforcement works." A vow to build a "big, beautiful wall" at the nearly 2,000-mile (3,218km) US-Mexico border was a signature promise of Trump's 2016 campaign.
sentences.article_title: Five ways Trump has changed immigration in the US

sentences.text: Progress on it has speeded up in his second term, boosted by $46.5bn (£34.7bn) in new funding from Trump's "One Big Beautiful" spending bill.
sentences.article_title: Five ways Trump has changed immigration in the US

sentences.text: According to government figures , external , about 644 miles of "primary wall" - closest to the border - existed before Trump returned to the White House, in addition to 75 miles of "secondary" wall set slightly further inside the US.
sentences.article_title: Five ways Trump has changed immigration in the US

sentences.text: Since then, 250 more miles of new wall have been completed, including primary, secondary and waterborne barriers, along with the technology that helps detect illegal crossings.
sentences.article_title: Five ways Trump has changed immigration in the US

sentences.text: An additional 1,443 miles of barriers are currently under construction.
sentences.article_title: Five ways Trump has changed immigration in the US

sentences.text: Experts, however, paint a more complex picture of what has been actually built rather than just improved or updated.
sentences.article_title: Five ways Trump has changed immigration in the US

sentences.text: Additionally, the impact the wall is itself having on the broader immigration figures is up for debate.
sentences.article_title: Five ways Trump has changed immigration in the US

sentences.text: "Since new wall construction has really begun in earnest, there has been no significant change in the number of people crossing the border," said Aaron Reichlin-Melnick, an immigration enforcement expert at the American Immigration Council.
sentences.article_title: Five ways Trump has changed immigration in the US

sentences.text: There is no indication the border wall has reduced migrant crossings, he added.
sentences.article_title: Five ways Trump has changed immigration in the US

sentences.text: The reduction has been more down to Trump's policies and messaging.
sentences.article_title: Five ways Trump has changed immigration in the US

sentences.text: Trump, for his part, continues to point to the wall as a successful policy - and continues to claim that Mexico paid for it.

sentences.text: "I'm the King of the Wall," Trump said at a rally in Kentucky on 17 October.

sentences.text: "By the way, Mexico did pay for that wall.

sentences.text: But the same data , external shows that a large chunk of the arrests involve people without criminal convictions.

sentences.text: Deportations have also ramped up significantly.

sentences.text: But the tactics used by ICE in US cities have made many Americans grow uncomfortable, including many of those who supported stricter restrictions broadly.

sentences.text: Haitian migrants changed this US town - Trump's deportation drive is reshaping it again Other legal pathways to come to live and work in the US have also been tightened up, through various policy changes.

sentences.text: Dozens of countries the Trump administration has deemed a security risk have been subject to a full or partial freeze on visas and travel.
sentences.article_title: Five ways Trump has changed immigration in the US

sentences.text: Enhanced vetting and new rules that send people residing in the US back to their home countries to apply for green cards has slowed that process down.

sentences.text: And in September 2025, a $100,000 fee on new H1-B visas for skilled workers , mostly held by Indians, stunned the US tech industry.

sentences.text: But some experts have cautioned the administration's aim of protecting American jobs, raising wages and stopping firms from outsourcing may prove elusive.
